subject: Slow convergence of a logistic regression with non-informative priors

messages.author: c6ba05975822c456
messages.subject: Slow convergence of a logistic regression with non-informative priors
parts:
Hi, Stan developers.

I'm trying to draw MCMC samples from a logistic regression model with Jeffrey's prior. 
I divide 10,000 binary response variable y into y1, y2, ..., y10, (that is, y1 ,..., y10 have 1,000 data) and 10,000×50 design matrix, X, into ten groups, X1, X2,..., X10 (that is, X1, ..., X10 are 1,000×50 matrix).
Then I implement MCMC with Stan for each divided data.

Now, when I implement the codes bottom, very slow convergence occasionally occurs for j=1,...,10 (in the R code bottom). The proportion of the slow convergence is one  in j=1,..,10.
Many implementation finish in 100 sec ~ 300 sec, however the slow convergence occasionally occurs and finish in 8,000 sec -10,000 sec.

I don't know why the slow convergence occurs nevertheless setting same initial values for all j=1,...,10.


Its Stan code is :

logit_for_subdataset.stan:
data {
        int<lower=0> N;
        int<lower=0> M;
        int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N];
        matrix[N,M] X;
}
parameters {
        vector[M] beta;
        real mu;
        real<lower=0> tau2;
}
model {
        y ~ bernoulli_logit(X*beta);
        beta ~ normal(mu,sqrt(10*tau2));
        increment_log_prob(-0.1*log(tau2));
}


And its R code is:

dim=50
num=10000
dev_num<-10




beta<-rnorm(dim,0,5)
X<-matrix(runif(num*(dim-1),-1,1), nrow=num, ncol=dim-1)
X<-as.matrix(data.frame(rep(1.0,num),X))
p<-exp(X%*%beta)/(1+exp(X%*%beta))
y<-c()
for(t in 1:length(p)){
 y[t]<-rbinom(1,1,p[t])
 }


inits <- list(list(beta=beta,mu=mean(beta),tau2=runif(1)),
              list(beta=beta,mu=mean(beta),tau2=runif(1)),
              list(beta=beta,mu=mean(beta),tau2=runif(1)),
              list(beta=beta,mu=mean(beta),tau2=runif(1))
)
for(j in 1:dev_num){
 subX<-X[(num/dev_num*(j-1)+1):(num/dev_num*j),]
 suby<-y[(num/dev_num*(j-1)+1):(num/dev_num*j)]

 d.dat<-list(N=num/dev_num,M=dim,X=subX,y=suby)
 result<-stan(file='logit_for_subdataset.stan',data=d.dat,iter=10000,chains=4,init=inits)
   
 assign(paste("result", j, sep=""),result)
}



Best regards.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Slow convergence of a logistic regression with non-informative priors
parts:
I'd suggest trying a non-centered parameterization.
Declare beta_raw as a vector parameter, and give it
density

beta_raw ~ normal(0, 1);

and then declare and define (either as transformed parameter or local
variable in the model block), a new vector

beta <- beta_raw * tau + mu;

to use in the regression, or just define it directly as

y ~ bernoulli_logit(X * (beta_raw * tau + mu));

Also, that prior on tau is very weak, so if you get extreme
values, you might want to make it tighter.

- Bob
